🔀 Multi-repo context Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf, Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts ## Linked repositories findings ### purrdf - PurRDF explicitly accepts `x-gmeow-english` and long private-use tags in both Turtle and N-Triples, so the new `RdfLiteral` language-tag emission is compatible with its parser. `[::Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf::]` (`crates/rdf/src/native_codecs/text_parse.rs:3617-3699`) - GTS literal validation also accepts `x-gmeow-english`; language tags are retained as literal identity rather than flattened. `[::Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf::]` (`crates/gts/src/model.rs:34-93`) - No direct consumers of the new `RdfSink` or `f64_decimal_lexical` names were found in PurRDF. ### gmeow-gts - GTS preserves private-use language tags in canonical payloads, but rejects them in projection/docs sections. Affect-ingest output using `x-gmeow-english` must therefore enter a canonical payload path, not a projection section. `[::Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts::]` (`python/src/gts/writer.py:57-76`, `python/tests/test_gts.py:661-675`) - GTS’s RDF codec tests require source decimal lexical forms such as `0.70` and `.5` to survive parsing/serialization, while generated numeric values may be normalized separately. The shared `f64_decimal_lexical` helper should remain limited to generated `f64` values, not parsed lexical text. `[::Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts::]` (`rust/tests/rdf_codecs.rs:461-500`) - No direct consumers of the new Rust helper names were found in gmeow-gts.
